**Finding submitted: deviation (IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data).**

- **What I checked:** Section 13 (the only ownership provision), the licence grant (§2) and use restrictions (§3), delivery/data conversion (§4), maintenance/Improvements (§10), confidentiality (§14), escrow (§16) and term (§17), plus the definitions of "Work", "Modifications" and "Improvements".
- **What is acceptable:** Garman keeping ownership of the Work, Improvements and Modifications is vendor platform ownership, and Sparkling has a perpetual licence while fees are paid (§17(a)) plus a perpetual, fully paid escrow licence to use and change the Codes on Garman default or loss of support (§16(b)) — that sits at the rule's fallback.
- **Why it still fails:** §13's ownership sweep extends to "all related materials, logos, and names provided pursuant to the terms of this Agreement" without limiting that to Garman-provided items, so it captures Sparkling's materials, branding and the Sparkling data Garman converts under §4(b). Nothing in the Agreement confirms Sparkling retains rights in its own data (§14 only makes it confidential) — the walk-away risk of Customer IP/data vesting in the Vendor.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** insert "by Garman" into the ownership sweep and add a sentence confirming Sparkling owns its data and materials, with no assignment to Garman and no joint ownership — leaving Garman's Software ownership untouched.
